name: Craft Planet
industry: CleanTech / Plastic Recycling & Sustainable Building Materials
what_they_do: Nigerian climate-tech social enterprise (operations in Bwari, Abuja and Kaduna, founded by Kabir Olaosebikan and Hanatu Abdulakeem) that collects and processes plastic waste into eco-bricks, interlocking tiles, and sustainable building materials while empowering women and community collectors.
recent_activity: 2026-11-10: Won NGN 5M (~$3,711) non-dilutive grant among Top 8 of the FMYD/NiYA-Cascador Founders Programme (https://techcabal.com/2026/11/10/cascador-niya-select-eight-founders/); 2026-11-06: Won NGN 40M Social Impact 1st place at Wema Bank Hackaholics 7.0 (https://www.instagram.com/p/DfebqWOoIRb); 2026-11-17: Featured in NiYA-Cascador Top 8 recap reel on @craftplanet_ltd Instagram (https://instagram.com/p/Df1rizGIRd8)
investors: Cascador / Nigerian Youth Academy (NiYA) / Federal Ministry of Youth Development
founder_or_marketing_contact: Kabir Olaosebikan (CEO) | Hanatu Abdulakeem (Co-Founder & Communication Lead) | contact@craftplanet.org | info@craftplanet.org | +234 813 215 5445
marketing_titles_found: NONE (craftplanet.org/teams/ lists Kabir Olaosebikan CEO, Hanatu Abdulakeem Co-Founder | Communication Lead, Aminat Abdulazeez COO, and two Plant Managers; no dedicated marketing, growth, or content title)
hiring_marketing_role: NO (no careers or open roles page on craftplanet.org)
unique_offer: Nigerian circular-economy manufacturer turning recovered plastic waste into eco-bricks and interlocking paving tiles claimed to be 3x stronger than concrete.
pitch_hook: Craft Planet won both NGN 40M at Wema Hackaholics 7.0 (2026-11-06) and NGN 5M from NiYA-Cascador (2026-11-10), yet craftplanet.org has no blog, still has broken WordPress theme links (ninzio.com) and typos ('Modular Hosing'), and lists no dedicated marketing or growth lead.
